question.problem:
Consider the matrix 
$T=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 10 \\ 4 & -10 & 2\end{aligned}].$ Find a basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(T).$
question.worked_solution:
In order to find a basis of $\text{Col}(T),$ we reduce the matrix $T$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 10 \\ 4 & -10 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 10 \\ 4 & -10 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 10 \\ 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-\frac{2}{5}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 10 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to linearly independent vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the $1$st, $2$nd and $3$rd columns are pivot columns.

Remember that we need to pick the pivot columns from the *original matrix*, not from the reduced one. 

The $1$st, $2$nd and $3$rd columns from the original matrix are ${t}_{1},$ ${t}_{2}$ and ${t}_{3}.$ So, a basis of $\text{Col}(T)$ is $\{{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}\},$ that is to say, 

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1 \\ -10\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 10 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\}.
$$
